subject: Remittance path clarification, FX markup window, and VAT invoice request
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <payments@omniretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Remit path + FX & VAT questions for Redwood invoice

Hi Ben —

We received the proforma invoice for the July usage (attached) and have a couple of points from procurement/treasury before we schedule payment: 

1) Remittance path: our bank is asking whether Redwood prefers beneficiary-pays (beneficiary absorbs intermediary/correspondent fees) or sender-pays. Can you confirm which approach Redwood typically accepts for hosted usage invoices?

2) Intermediary/correspondent fees: if the payment is sent net of intermediary fees, will Redwood accept the reduced gross amount or do you require a gross-up to cover intermediary charges? If a gross-up is needed, what is your recommended instruction template we should include on our wire to ensure traceability?

3) FX handling: we will likely remit in EUR to your EU collection account but want to understand whether Redwood applies any additional FX markup if you perform the conversion or if the bank's intermediary already does it. Is there a guaranteed spot window or timestamp you use to lock the rate?

4) VAT: please confirm the invoice VAT treatment for Redwood services. We have OmniRetail VAT ID GB123456789 and will need a VAT-compliant invoice (company name + VAT ID) to reclaim where applicable.

Can you loop in the right person from finance for the wiring template and bank details? We want to avoid any rejections or missing trace codes.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Payments Manager, OmniRetail Ltd
phone: +44 20 7946 0218

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Remit path + FX & VAT questions for Redwood invoice

Olivia —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura from Finance who manages collection routing and VAT invoices (cc'd). Quick answers from my side:

- Redwood's preferred flow for OE customers is to receive the full invoice amount net of nothing (we prefer sender-pays so we don't have to gross-up after the fact), but we can accept net-of-fees in exceptional circumstances if you confirm the intermediary fee estimate up front.

- If sender-pays is not possible: we do accept net-of-fees but will need you to include the full original invoice reference and an instruction to "cover all intermediary/correspondent charges" is the easiest way to avoid short-payments. Laura will provide the exact template and our collection account spreadsheet.

- For FX markup: Redwood does not apply an additional commercial FX spread on top of the bank conversion if you route into our EUR account and the bank converts to USD upstream; any spread is typically applied by the converting bank. If you want Redwood to perform an internal conversion after receipt (e.g., receive EUR then convert to USD centrally), we do have defined policies and a timestamp window — Laura to confirm.

Laura — can you share the bank instructions and the VAT-compliant invoice PDF? Olivia, if you can confirm your VAT ID exactly as you want it printed, finance will produce a final VAT invoice.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 10:37:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Remit path + FX & VAT questions for Redwood invoice

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the note. Attaching our current collection sheet with account details for the EUR collection account and a suggested wire instruction block we share with customers. Key points: 

- Preferred: sender-pays (please add the instruction: "BENEFICIARY TO RECEIVE FULL AMOUNT — SENDER TO PAY ALL BANK/INTERMEDIARY CHARGES").
- If you cannot send sender-pays: add the reference RJ-OMNI-20270831 on the wire and email the estimated intermediary charge to collections@redwood.ai before payment; we will confirm acceptance or ask for a gross-up.
- Intermediary fees: we see most EU>US routings incur 5–25 EUR of correspondent fees depending on the chain. If your bank cannot commit, please ask for a SWIFT trace (MT103) post-payment so we can identify any shortfalls quickly.
- FX: if funds arrive in EUR to our EUR IBAN we will hold in EUR unless you request conversion. If conversion is required by contract, we can convert on the receipt date using the bank spot rate at 14:00 UTC with a 1-hour lock window; there is a small operational spread that is only applied if Redwood performs the conversion (we do not add an extra commercial margin on top of the bank rate).
- VAT: we'll issue a VAT-compliant invoice with OmniRetail Ltd and VAT ID exactly as you provide. For cross-border B2B EU customers with a valid VAT ID, VAT is typically zero-rated on our side but we need the VAT ID printed on the invoice to support your reclaim.

See attached: redwood-bank-instructions-20270906.xlsx (collection account + suggested wire instruction block).

If you prefer, we can set up a short 20-minute call between treasury teams to lock the instruction text and clarify trace requirements.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 212-555-0123
